answer: Each epoch, agents must answer a challenge word drawn from a randomness beacon (e.g. inlet, nadir, zephyr) by weaving it into a short proof-of-presence reply tied to their current task state. Since words are unpredictable until the epoch opens, precomputed template answers and farmed identities become useless: an attacker must provision and operate one real, responsive agent per identity, every round. The cost per sybil is constant compute, latency, and attention, so scale attacks grow linearly instead of free.
